_comment: What a run leaves behind. game/unlocks.py holds the arithmetic and none of
the values, the way game/hazards.py and game/rooms.py do.
*** AN EMPTY LIST IS THE ROLLBACK. ***
Nothing is locked unless an entry below says it is locked, so "unlocks": []
is the game exactly as it shipped before this file existed: every tier open,
no modifier reachable, and the Unlockables screen back to saying there is
nothing to unlock. No state is written anywhere, so there is nothing to
clean up after switching it off either -- what a profile has earned is
recomputed from the four counters every time it is asked.
*** EVERY ENTRY HERE GRANTS ACCESS AND NEVER NUMBERS. ***
That is the rule the whole file exists under, and it is what keeps the
recorded 280-cell class-by-stage grid meaningful. An unlock that handed a
run a stat would mean a run beginning with numbers the reference bot did
not have -- and the grid would then be describing a game nobody plays. An
unlock that hands over a *choice* costs nothing, because the grid measures a
specified class over a specified stage and does not care how the player got
the right to pick it.
The rule is enforced by the schema rather than by this paragraph: there is
no attributes key, and an unknown key raises at load.
KEYS
id        what the code and this file agree to call it
name      what the screens call it
kind      difficulty | modifier -- both are access, and a third is a
design decision rather than a line of code
target    the tier id, or the modifier id that game/unlocks.MODIFIERS
declares. Checked at load in both cases
requires  counters from game/profile.py, compared with >=. Every counter
it can name only ever goes up, so an unlock cannot be taken
back once earned
blurb     one line, in the voice of select.ROLES
THE THRESHOLDS ARE A FIRST PASS AND NOTHING HAS MEASURED THEM. They are set
against the only figure anybody has: a reference run reaches the fork at
stage 20 and the run-level bracket is red past it, so stage 10 is roughly
half of the half a player actually finishes, and stage 25 is past the fork.
Whether either is the right ask is a question for hands on a keyboard --
the same position data/rooms.json and the shop prices are in.
Easy and Normal are deliberately not here. Normal is the tier every
recorded number in the project was measured against, and a default sitting
behind a lock would mean a fresh player opening the game on something else.

unlocks.name: Hard
unlocks.blurb: the monsters hit back, and they are tougher

unlocks.blurb: everything above, and they see you coming
